title: What is The Probability That A Random Graph With A Given Degree Sequence is Connected?
summary: An $n$-tuple $D=(d(1),\dots,d(n))$ is a \emph{feasible degree sequence} if there is a graph on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that $i$ has degree $d(i)$. Any such graph will have $m=\sum_{i=1}^n d(i)/2$ edges. Letting $G(D)$ be a graph chosen uniformly from those with the given degree sequence, we upper-bound the probability that $G(D)$ is disconnected based on the number of vertices of degree $d$ for small $d$, and develop a powerful tool for proving such bounds. If there are any vertices of degree zero the probability $G$ is disconnected is $1$, so we assume there are no such vertices. Our results…
